class.name: InputRouter
class.brief_description: Sends each raw input event to the player who owns the device it came from.
class.description: Created by [GFGDSceneTree] as [code]/root/InputRouter[/code], once, and never freed with a level. You do not add it yourself. It is one central node rather than an [code]_input[/code] override on each [PlayerController], for three reasons. A node only receives [code]_input[/code] for its own nearest ancestor [Viewport], so a router at the root sees every event exactly once no matter how many [SubViewport]s a split screen layout adds - per-controller handling would see each event zero or N times. An event from a device nobody owns has no controller to catch it, and press-to-join needs somewhere central to happen. And controllers are recreated per level, which would leave gaps in device assignment. It listens on [code]_input[/code], not [code]_unhandled_input[/code], on purpose: [PlayerInput] is a state machine, and if a [Control] swallowed a press but not the release the action would stay held forever. The router never marks input handled, so the GUI and every [code]_unhandled_input[/code] in the project still see events exactly as before. To stop gameplay input while a menu is open, disable the [InputComponent] instead.

signal.name: joypad_connected
signal.description: [param local_player] is the player that already owned this device slot, or [code]null[/code] for a pad nobody has claimed.

signal.name: joypad_disconnected
signal.description: The slot is released and everything it was holding is dropped, because nothing is ever going to deliver those releases. The [LocalPlayer] itself is kept, so plugging the pad back in and pressing a button resumes the same player rather than making a new one.

signal.name: unassigned_device_input
signal.description: A button was pressed on a device no player owns. Emitted before [method GameMode.try_join] is offered the slot, so this is the hook for a "press A to join" prompt.
